input.question: If the unreal engine is one of the most realistic and better looking game engines, why isn't it used more often in video games?
input.ground_truth: For indie dev: Game development is really, really hard already. If you don't need hyperrealistic graphics, why bother spending the extra hundreds of hours making detailed models, rigging them, creating animations, fine-tuning light sources, adjusting shader settings...? For established studios: Oftentimes, a studio will already have an engine they like to use, which they may have written themselves or bought from someplace else. Why bother learning a new engine and editor when you've already got experience with one that'll do the job fine? In general: It doesn't really make sense to say that the Unreal Engine, or any particular engine, is "one of the most realistic and better looking". That judgment is entirely subjective, not to mention massively in the developers' hands.

Question: If the unreal engine is one of the most realistic and better looking game engines, why isn't it used more often in video games?

response.prediction:
Okay, let’s imagine game engines are like toy kitchens. Some toy kitchens look really cool and have lots of fun features, but not everyone can play with them easily.

Unreal Engine is like a super fancy toy kitchen that makes really pretty cakes (the games look amazing!), but it’s also a bit harder to use and needs a bigger playroom (a stronger computer) to run smoothly. Some people want to make simple sandwiches quickly, so they use a different, easier toy kitchen that works on smaller tables (computers that aren’t as powerful).

Also, making things in the super fancy kitchen can take more time and learning. So, while Unreal Engine is great for making beautiful games, not everyone can or wants to use it for every game. Some games just need something simpler or something that works on more computers.
